# Results (generated by `scripts/make_figures.py` from `D:/IIT/Data_Science/outputs/runs/default`)

**Source: FULL run (configs/default.yaml, seed 42).** 72 run files; seed 42; 1000 bootstrap resamples; main alpha 0.01. All numbers below are read from the saved run files.

## Threshold-free metrics

- Novelty AUROC (vs known): how well the novelty statistic T(x) ranks hidden-attack flows above all known-class test flows (Normal and known attacks).
- Alarm AUROC: how well the normalised Normal-class score z_Normal(x) ranks hidden-attack flows above Normal test flows, i.e. whether the flow can be told apart from Normal traffic at all, novel or not (baseline: 1 - classifier probability of Normal).

## Main table (hybrid mode, alpha = 0.01, 95% bootstrap CIs)

Hybrid mode: a flow is *unknown* if its pooled conformal p-value is <= alpha; otherwise it gets the classifier's label. Detection = unknown + wrong known attack (not labelled Normal).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.0000 | 0 | 0.0000 | 0 | 0.0000 | 0 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| gmm | 202.8333 | 3651 | 463.8889 | 4578 | 536.1667 | 5218 | 0.0005 | 0.0099 | 0.0047 | 0.0451 | 0.0086 | 0.0784 |
| knn | 433.0556 | 3915 | 514.9444 | 4649 | 614.3333 | 5557 | 0.0010 | 0.0103 | 0.0048 | 0.0437 | 0.0095 | 0.0864 |
| pca | 0.0000 | 0 | 0.0000 | 0 | 2.5556 | 46 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0072 | 0.1304 |

**Resolution limit.** A conformal p-value can never be smaller than P_min = 1 / (n_final + 1). BH rejects the k smallest p-values only if p_(k) <= k q / m, so with the smallest p-values sitting at P_min, BH can reject only when at least about P_min * m / q test flows share that floor (m = number of test flows). The table gives, for each round, n_final, m, P_min, how many test flows are at the floor, and how many would be needed at each q. The floor count is a guide, not an exact condition: BH can also reject when the smallest p-values are just above the floor, as long as p_(k) <= k q / m holds (compare the 'flagged' and 'at floor' columns).

## Seed repeat (seeds 42, 43, 44; hybrid mode)

The rounds within one seed are not independent: they share the seed and all use the same Normal flows (Normal is never hidden). With the same seed, pairs of rounds often put the same Normal flows into the test split: over all pairs of rounds in seed 42, the share of Normal test flows in common ranges from 0.20 to 1.00 (median 0.65; about 0.20 would be expected by chance). The spread across rounds therefore understates run-to-run variation, and the seed repeat is the right check for the small excess of the pooled false unknown rate above alpha.

## Why novelty AUROC can fall below 0.5 (an explanation to check)

T(x) is the best match across all known classes (the minimum normalised score). A hidden attack whose flows lie in the dense core of a broad known class can therefore score as more typical than average known traffic, which pushes the novelty AUROC below 0.5. This is an explanation to check, not a result. Supporting numbers: the class each hidden flow fits best (detector-only best class).

## Runtime per detector (seconds per round)

`fit`: fitting on train (GMM includes fitting every reg_covar value and choosing on calib_norm; the baseline's fit is the classifier, which hybrid mode reuses for all detectors). `score`: scoring calib_norm, calib_final and test, and normalising. `bootstrap`: all CIs for both modes.

## Combined detectors (combo_<D>), from saved p-values, no re-fitting

Rule: a flow is unknown if min(P_D(x), P_baseline(x)) <= alpha / 2 (Bonferroni), otherwise it gets the classifier's label. By Bonferroni the false unknown rate on known flows is at most alpha, with no assumption about how the two p-values depend on each other. Novelty AUROC uses -min(P_D, P_baseline) as the score. Main alpha = 0.01; 95% bootstrap CIs.

## Duplicate-inflation check (optional experiment, no LOAO)

Accuracy and macro-F1 on the 20% test split; the last two columns give the share of test rows whose exact feature vector is also in the training split, and the share whose feature vector is in the training split under a different attack_cat.
